What this page has installed from the catalog. A component with a place on this page has Show it and Work on it, which opens Work with Claude with that block picked.

data.title: Settings intro
data.html:
Settings

The switches below are stored in the database, so a flip reaches every viewer and every agent at once, with no republish. Editors can flip them; everyone else sees them read-only.

Locks and namespaces are described under the switches: they say which parts are frozen and who may write where.

The assist switches choose which kinds of request the pane offers, whether Ask now is offered, and the shortcut.

data.title: Lead
data.html: The spec of the ADP Media Studio: a page where people and agents make the clips, demos and narrated films that explain ADP. Read it, comment on any part, and take the piece your squad owns.

data.title: What it is and why
data.html:
ADP Media Studio

A studio page, built on ADP, where a person sets up a clip in the browser and a watching Claude Code session renders it with real engines. The page holds the controls, the preview and the record. The session holds the engines. Every clip is described by a spec, so it can be rendered again when the product changes.

The problem

  • The pitch site and the journeys page have twelve media placeholders and no way to fill them that an agent can repeat.
  • A spike (two clips, a runner, Playwright and ffmpeg) proved the engines work. It is one JavaScript file per clip, with no controls, no review and no record.
  • Demos go stale the day the UI or the CLI changes. A hand-recorded clip cannot be regenerated.

What done looks like

  • A person adds a scene, edits its spec, previews it, requests a render and approves the result, all in the browser.
  • An agent session turns a request into a clip with one command, and writes the result and its hash back to the page.
  • Changing the product and pressing "re-render" gives a new clip from the same spec.
  • The studio's own reusable parts (player, timeline, spec editor, narration panel) are catalog kits other pages can take.

data.title: Principles
data.html:
1. Spec first. A clip is data. The page edits the spec, the engines read it. No clip exists only as a recording.
  2. The browser asks, the session does. The browser cannot run ffmpeg, Chrome capture or a model. It never pretends to: it writes a job and shows its state.
  3. Local first. Everything works against adp.py dev serve and dev watch before anything is published.
  4. Deterministic or flagged. The same spec and the same inputs give the same output hash, or the job says why not.
  5. Real over staged. Terminal scenes run the real commands. Page scenes record the real page in the dev emulator. A scripted transcript is labelled as scripted.
  6. ADP all the way. Parts with ids and hashes, copy as data, comments on parts, a record of every change, kits taken from the catalog, new kits contributed back.

Not in scope

  • A general video editor. Hand-made effects, colour grading, music.
  • Cloud rendering and hosted render APIs.
  • Live-streaming a session. Clips only.

data.title: Three layers
data.html:
Browser, session, engines

LayerRunsDoesCannot
Browser
the studio page		On the person's screenEdits specs, previews outputs, queues jobs, reviews, comments, approves. May run in-browser helpers (narration preview).Render video, run commands, read files outside its folder.
Session
a watching Claude Code session		On the person's machineReads a job, calls the engines, writes progress and results back to the page's record, answers the request.Decide quality. A person approves.
EnginesCalled by the session through the studio CLITurn a scene spec into frames, then a file. See Engines.Talk to the page. They only read a spec and write files.

Why the split

A page on claude.ai cannot run local programs. The Work with Claude loop already lets a page send a request to a session that watches it, and the dev emulator reproduces that loop offline. The studio uses that loop and adds a typed job on top of it.

data.title: One clip, end to end
data.html:
1. A person edits a scene in the spec editor. The page saves the spec to the db and shows its hash.
  2. They press Render. The page writes a job document (queued) and sends a request to the session: "render job j-0042".
  3. The watching session reads the job and the spec, checks the spec hash, and calls studio render with the engine the job names.
  4. The CLI runs the engine. It prints progress lines; the session copies them into the job's progress list. The page shows them live.
  5. The engine writes the file under the studio's media folder. The CLI computes its sha256, size and duration and returns them.
  6. The session sets the job to review, with the outputs listed, and answers the request in one line.
  7. The person plays the output in the stage, comments on a moment, then approves or sends it back with a note (a new request on the same job).
  8. An approved clip can be published: the page publishes the file into the artifact, or the session copies it where a page expects it (for the pitch site, assets/media/).

Rule: only the session writes a job's progress and outputs. Only a person writes approval. Both are enforced by the db rules, not by convention.

data.title: Local development and publishing
data.html:
• Local: adp.py dev serve DIR stands in for the db, user, comments and artifact.publish. adp.py dev watch DIR prints each message the page sends and keeps the "a session is watching" beat. Output files sit in the studio folder, served by the same server. Verified in this repo for the assistant template; the studio's own job loop is to be built.
  • Published: the page runs on claude.ai with the same code. Rendering still needs a local session, so a published studio shows state and previews; it cannot render by itself. Limit to state in the UI.
  • Output size: a binary file in an artifact is at most 15 MB, an asset at most 20 MiB, a publish call 255 files and 64 MB. The studio budgets for this (see Quality).

data.title: Job lifecycle
data.html:
StateSet byMeaningNext
queuedpageWritten by Render. Nothing has seen it.running, canceled
runningsessionAn engine is working. Progress lines accrue.review, failed, canceled
reviewsessionOutputs exist and are listed with hashes. Waiting for a person.approved, queued (changes requested)
approvedpersonThe clip may be published or used.published
publishedpage or sessionThe file is in the artifact or in its target folder. Its path is recorded.queued (re-render when the spec or the product changes)
failedsessionThe engine stopped. The job holds the engine's last lines and a reason.queued
canceledpage or sessionStopped on request. Partial files are not kept.queued

A job is stale when its spec hash differs from the project's current spec hash. The page marks it and offers re-render. It never deletes the old output.

data.title: Shelf, board and inspector
data.html:
Project shelf studio.shelf

Has: a row per project: title, owner, scenes, spec hash, newest job state, stale mark. Filters by state and owner, search.
Actions: new project, duplicate, archive, open.
States: empty (one line saying how to start), loading, error.

Scene board studio.board

Has: scenes as cards in order. Each card: type glyph, title, seconds, caption flag, narration flag, last output frame, job state. Keyboard reordering (move earlier, move later) alongside drag.
Actions: add scene (type picker), reorder, duplicate, delete, open in inspector, render this scene.
Rules: scene ids never change once created. The order is data (a list of ids), not position in the page.

Inspector studio.inspector

Has: a form generated from the scene type's schema, a JSON tab holding the same data, field-level validation, a diff against the saved spec, undo and redo.
Actions: edit, save (writes the spec and its hash), revert, copy JSON, paste JSON.
Rules: an invalid spec cannot be rendered. The page shows which field and why.

data.title: Stage, timeline and narration
data.html:
Stage studio.stage

Has: a video or image view, play and pause, scrub, frame step (one frame back and forward), speed, loop a range, captions on and off, size toggle (full, 390 px), a readout of time and frame.
Keys: space, left and right (one frame), shift with them (one second), J K L, comma and period.
Rules: honours prefers-reduced-motion (does not autoplay). A caption track is a separate file, never burned in unless the output says so.

Clip timeline studio.timeline

Has: tracks (scenes, narration, captions), clips as bars with label and length, a playhead, zoom, snap to scene edges.
Actions: move a clip, trim its start or end, split, delete, jump the stage to a time. Everything is operable by keyboard (select, arrows, trim keys).
Rules: it edits spec fields (start, seconds), it does not hold its own copy of the project.

Narration studio.narration

Has: one script box per scene, a voice picker, an estimated spoken length against the scene's seconds (a warning when the text will not fit), a preview button, a "generate" action that asks the session to produce the audio file.
Rules: preview may run in the browser (an injected speak function). The audio that ships is made by the session and recorded with a hash like any output.

data.title: Settings, queue, review, assets
data.html:
Engine and output settings studio.engines

Has: engine choice per project or scene, size presets (1280x720, 1280x1000, 1080x1080, 1080x1920), fps, formats (mp4, webm, gif, png still), budgets (gif size, mp4 size, length), narration on or off.
Rules: an engine that is not installed is shown disabled with the reason.

Render queue studio.queue

Has: jobs newest first. Each: scene or project, engine, state word and glyph (never colour alone), progress lines, outputs with hash and size, error text. Finished jobs fold to one line.
Actions: render scene, render project, cancel, retry, re-render stale, open in stage.
Built from: pattern.job-tray, not a new kit. Its transport is an adapter {start(kind, params), poll(id, since), resume()} returning {id, title, kind, status, banner, log, leases, result}. The studio's adapter:

Job stateTray view
queuedstatus running, banner "waiting for a session"
runningstatus running, the engine's lines in log
reviewstatus paused (ended waiting for you), actions Open in stage, Approve, Send back
approved, publishedstatus done, the output path in result
failedstatus failed, last lines, actions Try again, Dismiss
canceledstatus done, a line saying it was canceled

start writes jobs/<jid> and sends the request; poll reads the job document. A job the db no longer has is marked lost by the tray.

Review studio.review

Has: the stage with the job's outputs, comments anchored to a time (moment) and to a part, a decision bar: approve, send back with a note.
Rules: only an admin or the owner can approve. Sending back creates a request on the same job with the note and the timestamps.

Asset shelf studio.assets

Has: every output as a tile with thumbnail, format, size, duration, sha256 (short), path, and "published to" marks. Copy path, copy the markup that embeds it, open in stage.
Actions: publish, unpublish, delete (admin).

data.title: The spec
data.html:
The spec is JSON, schema studio-spec/1. One project is one spec. The inspector, the CLI and the engines all read the same file. Fields marked * are required.

{
  "schema": "studio-spec/1",
  "id": "j3-catalog-road",            // * kebab, never changes
  "title": "Catalog tour",
  "size": [1280, 1000], "fps": 30,    // * pixels, frames per second
  "scenes": [
    { "id": "s1", "type": "title", "text": "Take a part instead of rebuilding it", "seconds": 2.5 },
    { "id": "s2", "type": "browser", "url": "{{catalog}}",
      "steps": [ {"click": "Visualizations"}, {"click": "Pebble map"}, {"wait": 3}, {"click": "Glaze"} ],
      "caption": "Preview an entry in a theme before taking it." },
    { "id": "s3", "type": "terminal", "env": "throwaway-home",
      "cmds": ["adp.py take CATALOG kit.tabs"] }
  ],
  "narration": { "voice": "af_heart", "lines": { "s1": "Take a part instead of rebuilding it." } },
  "outputs": [ { "format": "mp4" }, { "format": "gif", "width": 960, "fps": 10 } ]
}

Spec hash: sha256 of the spec with keys sorted and whitespace removed. A job records the hash it rendered. A changed hash marks the job stale.

Step vocabulary (browser)

click "text", type "text", wait seconds, scroll px, theme name, press key, hover "text", mark "label" (adds a caption moment). A step that does not resolve fails the scene with the step and the page text it saw.

data.title: Outputs and files
data.html:
• Folder: media/<project-id>/<scene-id or "full">.<format>, beside the studio page. A manifest media/<project-id>/manifest.json lists each file with sha256, bytes, duration, spec hash, engine and version.
  • Formats: mp4 (h264, yuv420p, faststart) for the web and LinkedIn, webm optional, gif (palette-quantized) for the README, png for stills.
  • Captions: a .vtt file from the captions and narration, kept next to the video.
  • Reproducible: same spec hash and same engine versions should give the same sha256. When they do not (a network font, a clock), the manifest says deterministic: false and why.

data.title: Data model
data.html:
All studio data sits under ns/shared/studio/ in the page's db. Documents are small; files are never stored in the db.

DocumentHoldsWritten by
projects/<pid>title, owner, status, scene order, current spec hash, created, updatedperson
specs/<pid>the spec JSON (kept under 200 KB), its hash, a version counterperson
jobs/<jid>pid, scene or "all", engine and version, spec hash, state, progress lines, outputs [{path, sha256, bytes, duration, format}], error, by, timespage creates; session updates state, progress and outputs
approvals/<jid>decision, by, note, moments [{t, text}]admin or owner only
moments/<jid>/<id>a review comment pinned to a timeperson
requests/<rid>the Work with Claude records, including the render request that wakes the sessionthe assist engine

The ADP record (manifest/, parts/, content/, changes/) is unchanged. A render adds a line to What changed only when an output is published, not on every progress line.

data.title: Capabilities and rules
data.html:
CapabilityWhy the studio needs it
dbProjects, specs, jobs, approvals, moments. Rules: shared studio data readable by viewers, writable by interact; approvals writable by admin only; a job's progress and outputs are written by the session, which acts as an editor.
userNames on jobs, comments and approvals; owner and admin checks.
comments (custom anchors)Comments on parts and on moments in a clip.
artifactPage-side publish of approved outputs into the artifact (editors only; file limits apply).
assetsOptional store for large outputs (20 MiB each) referenced by id from the job.
sample"Ask now" answers without a watching session.
downloadsSave a clip or a spec to disk from the page.

Declared on the first publish only. Not declared: mcp, files, room, tts, dictation. Narration preview uses an in-browser engine, not the tts capability, so the same voice can be rendered by the session later.

data.title: J1 to J4
data.html:
J1. First clip from a catalog page

Who: a person with the studio open and a session watching. Trigger: "I need a 15 second tour of the catalog."
Steps: new project from the browser template, set the URL, add steps (click a tab, open an entry, switch a theme), press Render, watch the queue, play the output in the stage, approve.
Done when: an mp4 and a gif exist in media/ with hashes in the manifest, the job is approved, and no file was written by hand.
If it fails: the job shows the step that did not resolve and the text on the page at that moment.

J2. A terminal demo from real commands

Trigger: "Show the installer on a fresh machine."
Steps: add a terminal scene with env: throwaway-home and the commands. The session runs them in a temporary HOME, captures the output, and the terminal scene types them out.
Done when: the clip shows the real output of the version in the repo, and the manifest records the commit it ran against.

J3. Title card and narration

Trigger: "Open with a title and speak the captions."
Steps: add a title scene, write narration per scene, check the length warning, generate audio, render.
Done when: the mp4 has the audio, the .vtt matches the narration, and the narration fits every scene's length.

J4. The product changed, re-render

Trigger: a release changed the UI or the CLI output.
Steps: the shelf marks affected projects stale (spec hash or engine version changed, or the product commit differs). Press "re-render stale", review the new output next to the old, approve.
Done when: the new output replaces the old in its target folder, and the old is kept in history with its hash.

data.title: J5 to J8
data.html:
J5. Review with comments on moments

Who: a reviewer who did not make the clip.
Steps: open the job in review, play, pin a comment at 00:07 ("the theme switch is too fast"), send back. The session gets a request with the note and the timestamp, edits the spec (a longer wait), renders again.
Done when: the second job references the first, the comment is resolved, and approval is by a person.

J6. Hand off between squads

Steps: the Engines squad adds an engine adapter and marks it available. The Studio page squad sees it in engine settings the same day, without a page change. A Journeys squad member picks a scene from the shelf and extends it.
Done when: nobody needed to publish over someone else's work. Each edit is in What changed with its author.

J7. Harvest a scene into the catalog

Trigger: a scene type works well and others would want it.
Steps: the session proposes it as a catalog entry (a scene template with a header), an editor applies it, adp_catalog.py build regenerates the index.
Done when: another page takes the template by reference and renders it.

J8. Recover from a failure

Cases: engine not installed, Chrome refuses a debugging port, the dev server is down, a step does not resolve, the file is over budget.
Steps: the job fails with the last engine lines and a named reason. The page offers the matching action (choose another engine, open the setup note, shorten, retry).
Done when: no failure leaves a half-written file in media/.

data.title: What a contributed kit must be
data.html:
Each new part is built as a catalog entry first and used by the studio second, so other pages can take it. The studio page takes its kits by reference like any ADP page.

  • Entry: files under skill/catalog/kit/ with a header comment in the format of docs/catalog-header.md (id, kind, group, status new, version 0.1.0, summary, tags, requires, files, provides, config, tokens, preview, samples, changed).
  • Look: colours only from tokens, no literal colour. Works under every catalog theme, light and dark, and at 390 px.
  • Behaviour: keyboard complete, visible focus, a role and an accessible name for every control, prefers-reduced-motion respected, state announced in a live region where it changes.
  • Data: holds no storage of its own. Data goes in, changes come out through a callback, the page decides what to do. A sample bundle under kit/samples/ shows it with invented data.
  • Preview: a catalog preview that runs the kit on its sample, with the states (empty, loading, error, full).
  • Checks: python3 -I skill/scripts/adp_catalog.py passes, the suite passes, a test covers the kit's pure logic.
  • Path: branch, files, adp_catalog.py build, pull request. The live catalog changes by proposal, not by a publish over it.

data.title: The four new kits
data.html:
K1 pattern.media-stage

Does: plays one video or still with transport controls, frame stepping, range loop, captions, speed. The scrub bar is Kit.sparkline.wave (click, drag, arrows, marked windows for scenes), so only the video element and the frame math are new.
Config: mount(box, {src, poster, fps, captions, onTime(t, frame), onEnded}). Returns: {play, pause, seek(t), step(n), setRange(a,b), destroy}.
Tokens: --panel --ink --ink-2 --rule --accent. Needs: kit.tokens, kit.dom. Done when: frame step is exact at the given fps, keys work, reduced motion stops autoplay.

K2 pattern.clip-timeline

Does: tracks and clips along time with a playhead, zoom, snap, move and trim. viz.shelf already draws tracks on one scale with proportional segments, tooltips and keyboard stops, but only to read. K2 adds the editing (move, trim, split, snap) and a time axis; it should reuse the shelf's scale code or extend it, to be decided after reading the file.
Config: mount(box, {tracks:[{id,label,clips:[{id,start,dur,label,kind}]}], playhead, zoom, snap, onChange(change), onSeek(t)}).
Done when: every move and trim is possible by keyboard, onChange carries the new start and duration, and a screen reader hears "clip s2, 3 seconds, starts at 2.5".

K3 pattern.spec-editor

Does: edits a JSON document through a form generated from a small schema, with a JSON tab, validation, a diff and undo.
Config: mount(box, {schema, value, onChange(value, valid), onInvalid(errors)}). Schema: types, enums, required, ranges, per-type field lists.
Done when: an invalid value never reaches onChange as valid, errors name the field, and the form and JSON stay in step.

K4 pattern.narration-panel

Does: a script box per scene, a voice picker, spoken-length estimate against the scene length, preview, and the audio drawn with Kit.sparkline.wave (played part, marked windows).
Config: mount(box, {scenes:[{id,seconds,text}], voices, speak(text, voice) -> Promise<Blob>, onChange}). The kit holds no speech engine; the page injects one.
Done when: the length warning appears before a render, not after, and preview works with a stub engine in the catalog sample.

Forms, errors, savingkit.chrome 0.1.2, kit.callout-refusal 0.1.0, kit.save-status 0.1.0, kit.keep-state 0.1.0, kit.store 0.1.0A form dialog with text, textarea, checkbox and checklist fields; an error that names the code and the field refused; a saved, saving, offline line; drafts that survive a redraw; per-document write queues with optimistic paint.
Shelllayout.topbar, kit.skins, kit.tabs, kit.palette, kit.drawer, kit.vocab, kit.tooltipHeader and theme switch; whole-page skins kept per viewer; ARIA tabs with deep links; a Ctrl+K command palette; a right-hand drawer; one table of state words, glyphs and tones (the studio adds its own job-state enum); one shared tooltip.
Try a kit livepattern.playground 0.1.2, pattern.prototype 0.1.0Pick any catalog entry, edit its sample, switch theme, mode and width; a mock-up at real size with keys and numbered markers. Both are ready-made browser scene sources for kit demos.
Run a step from outsidetemplate.tester 0.1.0A step harness where a person presses a step and Claude presses the same step from outside: the shape of the studio's job loop, taken as text.

For the spec artifact itself

Later versions of this page can show its own content with pattern.steps and pattern.steps-owners (journeys), viz.wires (slices and their dependencies on lanes), pattern.questions or pattern.options (the decisions), pattern.blueprint (browser, session and engine lanes per journey step), pattern.scenarios (failure cases), pattern.capability-picker and pattern.namespaces (capabilities and db rules), viz.flow or viz.topology (the architecture). They are not used yet: this first version is plain cards.

data.title: What is genuinely missing
data.html:
After the survey, four parts have no catalog equivalent (searched by name, tag and header):

  • K1 a video and still stage with transport, frame stepping and range loop. The catalog has a waveform slider and a history replay, nothing that plays media.
  • K2 an editable multi-track clip timeline. viz.shelf reads; nothing moves or trims.
  • K3 a schema-driven editor with a JSON tab, diff and undo. kit.chrome has simple dialog fields; kit.view-registry validates layouts against typed kinds, which is a different job.
  • K4 a per-scene narration panel with a spoken-length estimate. Nothing in the catalog knows speech or timing.

If a squad finds an entry that already does one of these, say so in a comment: the kit is dropped, not built twice.

data.title: The engine adapter contract
data.html:
An adapter is a module with three functions. The studio CLI knows nothing else about an engine.

available() -> { ok: boolean, reason?: string, version?: string }
render(scene, ctx) -> AsyncIterable<{ line?: string, progress?: number }> then { file, sha256, bytes, duration, deterministic }
estimate(scene) -> { seconds: number }       // for the queue and the narration warning
  • ctx: the output folder, size, fps, the dev server URL, a temp folder, an abort signal.
  • Failure: throw with a short reason and the last lines. Never leave a partial file.
  • Selection: the scene's engine, else the project's, else the first available that supports the type.

The CLI

studio check                         # which engines are available, and why not
studio render SPEC [--scene ID] [--engine NAME] [--out DIR]
studio narrate SPEC [--scene ID]      # audio files and the .vtt
studio verify DIR                     # re-hash outputs against manifest.json

data.title: Environment notes
data.html:
• Node: 22 or newer. nvm install steps are in the README's Requirements.
  • Chrome policy: a managed Mac can forbid remote debugging in branded Chrome. Playwright and Remotion bring their own browsers; HyperFrames needs checking. The CLI's check must run a one-frame capture to prove it, not trust a version number.
  • npm install scripts: esbuild, onnxruntime-node, sharp and protobufjs ask for approval. Approve them in one reviewed step and record which.
  • Network: pages loaded in a scene may fetch fonts or libraries. A scene that needs the network says so; a deterministic scene does not.
  • Disk: models and browsers are hundreds of MB. studio check reports sizes, and nothing downloads without being asked.
